criteria.quote: "Squirtle's shell was built for more than defense."
criteria.revision: Open with the concrete contradiction instead: "Squirtle’s shell protects it—but its grooves are also built to cut water resistance." This preserves the evidence while making the reveal more distinctive immediately.

criteria.quote: "Its rounded shape and grooves minimize resistance in water."
"Why would a protective shell be shaped for speed?"
criteria.revision: Make the open loop more precise and delay the answer: "If Squirtle’s shell is armor, why does it have rounded grooves?" Then reveal that they minimize water resistance in the later scene.

criteria.quote: "Its shell starts soft, then soon hardens into resilient armor." / "Yet the Pokédex says this shell is not merely protection."
criteria.revision: Combine the hardening and protection setup so it does not spend two consecutive scenes establishing armor: change scene 2 to "It starts soft, then hardens until prodding fingers bounce off. That sounds like the whole purpose—until you look at its shape." This moves directly from proof of defense into the speed reveal.

criteria.quote: "Yet the Pokédex says this shell is not merely protection."
criteria.revision: Put the reversal in the same line as the visual detail: "The surprise is on the surface: Squirtle’s rounded shell and grooves minimize water resistance." This makes the perspective shift land on the specific fact rather than the general teaser.

criteria.quote: "Squirtle's shell was built for more than defense." / "Yet the Pokédex says this shell is not merely protection."
criteria.revision: Remove or rewrite scene 3 because it restates scene 1’s central claim. Use it to introduce the unanswered physical detail instead: "The clue is its rounded shape—and the grooves across its shell."

criteria.quote: "That lets Squirtle swim at high speeds, not just hide."
criteria.revision: Make the final reveal resolve both halves of the setup in one sharper contrast: "The same shell that becomes resilient armor also has a rounded, grooved surface that minimizes water resistance—enabling Squirtle to swim at high speeds."

criteria.quote: "In danger, would you trust its shell or its speed?"
criteria.revision: Ground the choice more directly in the documented actions: "When threatened, Squirtle can draw into its shell and spray water—so would you shelter in the shell or try to use its high-speed swimming?"
